paragraphs.source_en: 1. Identify a Quadrant II activity you know has been neglected in your life—one that, if done well, would have a significant impact in your life, either personally or professionally. Write it down and commit to implement it. 2. Draw a time management matrix and try to estimate what percentage of your time you spend in each quadrant. Then log your time for three days in fifteen-minute intervals. How accurate was your estimate? Are you satisfied with the way you spend your time? What do you need to change? 3. Make a list of responsibilities you could delegate and the people you could delegate to or train to be responsible in these areas. Determine what is needed to start the process of delegation or training. 4. Organize your next week. Start by writing down your roles and goals for the week, then transfer the goals to a specific action plan.

units.source_en: ## NEW INSIGHTS ON HABIT 3: PUT FIRST THINGS FIRST

paragraphs.source_en: Many years ago at a family gathering, my dad announced, “I have the greatest trip planned. Are you ready? We are going to Germany!” My siblings and I got all excited and asked, “When?” And he replied, “In three years!” We took out our planners (we didn’t have smartphones yet) and realized that none of us had a calendar that booked out that far!

paragraphs.source_en: Even with Dad’s grueling schedule, we did a lot of things together because he was a master at putting first things first and blocking out time in advance. He would say, “Families don’t do things together because they don’t plan ahead.” He’d plan weeks, months, years, even decades ahead. I think it is safe to say that I am really close to all my siblings because of this one practice.
